title: CI, CD, and CT need different evidence
lead: Integration, delivery, deployment, and training automate different responsibilities.
bullets: CI: integrate changes and run code, contract, and path checks.
Delivery: keep a compatible change ready for an approval decision.
Deployment: automatically release changes passing the defined policy.
CT: train and evaluate candidates; completion is not production approval.
example: A connector repair can use CI/CD while retaining M1. Retraining is not required for every pipeline change.
takeaway: Automation executes policy; it does not make acceptance criteria identical.

title: Candidate training ends before promotion
lead: A registry stores candidate evidence; a separate release decision controls production use.
bullets: Reproducibility: record data, code, configuration, and artifacts.
Evaluation: compare candidate evidence against the baseline and relevant cohorts.
Registration: preserve identity and lineage for review.
Promotion: authorize a specific compatible set with recovery planned.
example: M2 remains a candidate until reviewed. M1 remains the approved scoring artifact during the CRM repair.
takeaway: The registry is part of governance, not the whole approval process.

title: Repair the input path; retain M1 when appropriate
lead: The CRM incident requires a verified source repair, not an assumed new model.
bullets: Repair the source or preparation defect.
Version the reviewed fix and compatible configuration.
Re-run under a new execution identity and validate the complete path.
Publish only after the configured evidence and approval requirements pass.
example: B017 is the held attempt. B017-R1 links the reviewed fix, compatible M1, validation evidence, and publication approval.
takeaway: A successful fix needs evidence at the consumer boundary, not only a passing connector test.

title: Trace the prediction and the decision
lead: Lineage connects input evidence, execution, approval, and downstream action.
bullets: Prediction identity links customer, time, and target window.
Execution evidence identifies compatible code, features, model, and config.
Decision evidence records policy version and action.
Access controls protect sensitive reconstruction material.
example: An investigator can trace Ana’s original score and the campaign’s separate no-contact or contact decision.
takeaway: A model version alone cannot reconstruct the full decision.

title: Recovery restores a compatible path
lead: Rehearse restoration before release, and verify it at the consumer boundary.
bullets: Know the target: identify the last compatible release or validated fallback.
Rehearse: test the recovery procedure before relying on it.
Restore the set: include data meaning, runtime, and configuration.
Verify: inspect stored scores and actual consumer behavior.
example: Rolling M1 back cannot repair a CRM field that is still missing; the input path must be restored.
takeaway: Handoff to security: who may read, change, approve, or operate these paths?
